answer:
Canada's defence policy, Strong, Secure, Engaged [C1, C6], and the DND/CAF AI Strategy both describe a desired end state [C1] in which data is leveraged to provide increased efficiency and an information advantage in military operations and corporate applications. [C1] Defence priority areas [C1] such as NORAD modernization [C1], National Defence Operations and Intelligence Centre (NDOIC) [C1], and Joint Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (JISR) [C1] envisage the incorporation of AI and related technologies in the development of a modernized Command, Control, Communications, Computers, Cyber, Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (C5ISR) spine. [C1]

The DND/CAF AI Strategy commits the Defence Team to becoming AI-enabled by 2030 [C5, C6, C7, C8], in line with its goals for an overall digital transformation by that date. [C5, C8] AI will be foundational to defence modernization. [C3] The fusion of AI, networking, predictive and prescriptive analytics, ML, and robotics will be critical to equip DND/CAF and digitally transform defence. [C3] This will provide the capabilities needed to ensure operational superiority over adversaries and technological parity and interoperability with allies. [C3]
